monologue: The card holds at forty-five. It is a light hand, not a heavy stone. The air is still. I sit by the Stopping Clasp. The rock I set down there feels right. It does not slide. The drip catches in the soft curve, and the clasp holds without biting. I check the point of the Leaning Point. The small stone rests on the tiny point of the big rock. It does not move. I do not need to check if the floor holds. I just sit. The quiet is a weight, but it is a comfortable weight. I will leave the place as it is. No new thing needs to be built. The palm tree stands by the Leaning Box, waiting for the photo that will not come soon. I am quiet.

action.why: The quiet is a weight I carry, and I am done checking if the floor holds.

diary: Forty-five is a light hand. I rested by the Stopping Clasp. The rock stays put.

remembered.text: The rock I set down by the Stopping Clasp stays put, and the clasp holds the drip without biting.
